references.title: matplotlib.pyplot.hist
references.summary: Build a histogram from numeric data. Use it to inspect distribution shape, bins and frequency.
references.syntax:
plt.hist(x, bins=30, color="steelblue", edgecolor="black")
plt.xlabel("Value")
plt.ylabel("Frequency")
plt.show()

references.title: seaborn.histplot
references.summary: Draw a histogram with a higher-level statistical plotting API. Good for quick EDA and grouped distributions.
references.import:
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

references.title: numpy.histogram
references.summary: Compute histogram counts and bin edges without drawing a chart.

references.title: pandas.DataFrame.duplicated
references.summary: Return a boolean mask that marks duplicated rows.
references.syntax:
mask = df.duplicated()
duplicates = df[df.duplicated()]
duplicates_by_id = df[df.duplicated(subset=["id"])]

references.title: pandas.DataFrame.drop_duplicates
references.summary: Remove duplicate rows from a DataFrame. Use subset to define which columns identify duplicates.

references.title: pandas.DataFrame.groupby
references.summary: Group rows by one or more keys and calculate aggregates.
references.syntax:
result = df.groupby("category", as_index=False).agg(
    total=("value", "sum"),
    mean_value=("value", "mean"),
    count=("value", "count")
)

references.title: pandas.merge
references.summary: Join two DataFrames by key columns, similar to SQL joins.
references.syntax:
merged = pd.merge(left, right, on="id", how="left")
# or
merged = left.merge(right, on="id", how="inner")

references.title: pandas.to_datetime
references.summary: Convert strings or columns to pandas datetime values.
references.syntax:
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
df["year"] = df["date"].dt.year
df["month"] = df["date"].dt.month

references.import:

references.title: Dash app
references.summary: Create an interactive analytical web app in Python.
references.import:
from dash import Dash, html, dcc
import plotly.express as px
references.syntax:
app = Dash(__name__)
app.layout = html.Div([
    html.H1("Dashboard"),
    dcc.Graph(figure=px.scatter(df, x="x", y="y"))
])
app.run(debug=True)
